title: Starting on trumpet: cousin Ran Briscoe's horn and early lessons
summary: De De got his first trumpet at about fifteen from a cousin on the road via her sister, then took lessons; the sister later played in Sweetheart's Rhythm girl band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about your education. Did you have any music in school at all?

No, no, no, no, no. It started, I had a niece, cousin rather, on the road years ago. I was around about fifteen. With a regular, a minister or a troop, whatever they call it, traveling around, you know. And she played trumpet. In other words, taking sick or what, she sent the trumpet to her sister, which is Nelisco, today her name is Nelisco Briscoe. And she began to learn on the trumpet. The sister did a twentieth century, it was called a twentieth century trumpet. It was a brass instrument, cornet. On it. And in other words, she gave me, got this guts and she gave me the horn and I picked up the horn and started to play and you know, practicing, you know, by here, by here, by here. And then I went to lessons. What I call it, I told you, Charlo, Charlo Nee at the time. He was a letter carrier and a music teacher at the time. And that's how I started my music.
What was your cousin's name that had a trumpet on the road?
Ran. Ran. We used to call her Ran. Ran Briscoe.
Ran Briscoe.

Well they were years back, yeah. You know some girl troupe. Then when she sent her sister to horn, her sister learned enough to play to join Sweetheart's Rhythm. That was a colored girl band we had here too. They done well and they broke up years back too. The sister learned to dance from her. That's Naliska. That's Naliska. She don't play anymore. Give it up. California, so where I know. They had Sweetheart's Rhythm. It was a known band here at one time. You know, colored man. Girl band. One time.
Were they mostly girls from here?
All girls from here, yeah. Mostly from here.
Do you remember the names of any of those?
No, I wasn't sure.
You better chip that noise.
I got the trumpet from her and that's how I started.
And who was it?
That's the way we're third handed when I got it.
And what minstrel shows did your cousins play with?
Oh I couldn't even tell you that.
You don't know anything about that?
I went on the road most of the time and I didn't know anything too much about no music and shows and stuff at the time, you know.
And your cousin Rand was from here too or not?
Yeah, she was from here. Oh yeah. She had left here as a kid I guess, you know, left home.
You don't hear of many women trumpet players now. No. No. I sure don't. They had one in Chicago.
Sometime I heard a big band on the radio, oh, been a good while back. Not from here though, I know they're not from here. There's some nice, nice music.
